description: Headcount 243, equal to 227.8 full-time equivalent posts, as at 12 October 2026, with 109 in technical roles and 134 in other roles, in written parliamentary answers UIN 30890 (as corrected on 22 October 2026) and UIN 33991. The answer to UIN 30890 first gave 241, equal to 211.2 full-time equivalent posts. Asked for current and planned staffing, the government gave the current figures and said future staffing is managed in line with the budget allocated in the Spending Review.
Japan's Cabinet Office reports about 200 or more staff, including 90 specialists.

More than 140 staff, including over 40 in the AI safety unit, most of them with technical profiles (Commission answer to parliamentary question P-001672/2026). The AI Office's own page (updated 8 September 2026) gives more than 125 staff; the answer to Parliament is kept as the more specific source.

The Cabinet Office of Japan's April 2026 comparison reports about 30 US staff as of 2024 and a target of 80, with no target date. Japan AISI's January 2025 English overview gives the same approximate total and target. No US primary confirmation of that historical total and target was located.

ZDNet Korea reported 34 US personnel and a plan to expand to 80, citing materials from South Korean lawmaker Lee Jeong-heon's office. The report gives the count as current in September 2026, its publication month. No US primary confirmation of the count, staffing scope or target date was found.

The 7 April 2026 Cabinet Office document's comparison table gives 31 including concurrent appointments from IPA and RIKEN. The target of 60 is from a governing-party (LDP) recommendation of 19 December 2025 that the document reproduces, which asks to expand urgently from the then current 30; a separate government plan has ministries second staff from April to around July 2026. The prime minister's instruction of 19 December 2025 aims for 200, with no target date stated. The count is the one the document gives as current in April 2026, its publication month; it states no separate headcount date.
Just over 30 staff including concurrent appointments within IPA, of whom 20 are dedicated staff. The lower-bound total is not a dedicated-only count.

A member of the National Assembly said at the October 2026 parliamentary audit that the institute's staff had grown from 26 to 38 and is still short of peer institutes, as reported in the press. ZDNet Korea reported, from ministry and institute material, that the evaluation lab has 7 staff, 6 of them technical evaluators. The count is the one given as current at the October 2026 audit. No official current headcount was found. The technical count of at least 6 is the evaluation lab's technical evaluators, which is only part of the institute. At the parliamentary audit of 20 October 2026, asked whether only six staff can analyse AI models' risks and run hacking simulations, the president of ETRI, the institute's host, answered that six people handle this work, as reported by Money Today.
The science ministry's release dated 27 November 2024 lists 12 institute staff.

Headcount 29, equal to 27.4 full-time equivalent posts, as the institute's General Manager told a Senate estimates hearing on 29 October 2026 (uncorrected proof Hansard). Asked how many are in technical roles, she said seven staff, 6.4 full-time equivalent, work on evaluating models and six, 5.8 full-time equivalent, are in the regulatory engagement team. The technical count of at least 7 is the staff evaluating models.

25 staff, about half of them technical, as the institute's General Manager told the Joint Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence on 18 September 2026 (uncorrected proof Hansard). The technical count of about 12 is derived from these figures: half of 25, rounded down.
